newsitem.title: USA: Gannett to sell radio stations for $304 mln.
newsitem.headline: Gannett to sell radio stations for $304 mln.

text.p: Gannett Co Inc's radio broadcast unit has agreed to sell all of its five radio stations to Evergreen Media Corp for approximately $304 million, the companies announced Thursday.
Under the deal, Evergreen will acquire Gannett's WGCI-AM and WBCI-FM in Chicago, KHKS-FM in Dallas and KKBQ-AM and KKBQ-FM in Houston.

Separately, Evergreen, an Irving, Texas-based radio broadcast company, said it has agreed to sell three radio stations -- WPNT-FM and WLUP-FM in Chicago and KDFC-FM in San Francisco -- to Bonneville International Corp, a private Salt Lake City-based company, for $205 million in cash.

Evergreen said the transactions are part of its divestiture and portfolio initiatives it was implementing as a result of its February agreement to acquire Chancellor Broadcasting Corp in a stock swap.

That deal created Chancellor Media Corp, which would become the largest company in the nation devoted to radio broadast. Both Evergreen and Chancellor said they would sell stations in markets to meet federal ownership limitations.
As of April 8, both companies have announced the sale of radio stations in deals valued at $313 million and continue to pursue divestiture plans.
Evergreen said the most recent transactions would bring it into federal ownership requirements for Chicago, one of the nation's busiest radio markets.
Scott Ginsburg, chairman and chief executive officer of Evergreen and CEO of Chancellor Media, said the deal aims to fortify the new company's presence in the nation's leading radio markets.
Ginsburg noted that acquisitions from Gannett and its earlier deal to buy the radio division of Viacom Inc were some of the country's best radio station properties.

The transaction with Gannett is expected to close in the fourth quarter, while the deal with Bonneville is scheduled to close in the third quarter, both this year, the companies said. Both transactions are subject to approval by the Federal Communications Commission.

After the sale of its radio stations, Gannett Broadcasting said its operations will consist of 16 televisions stations covering 16 percent of the nation, cable operations in five states and alarm security services.
Gannett, based in Arlington, Va., also publishes, USA Today, part of its holdings of 91 newspapers.
